newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi official stabbed on street-Japan police.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi official stabbed on street-Japan police.

text.p: The official in charge of customer complaints at Japan's scandal-hit Yamaichi Securities was stabbed to death on a Tokyo street on Thursday while returning home from work, police said.
A police spokesman identified the executive as Koichiro Tarutani, 57, who handled complaints from investors about share transactions made for them by the company.

"Tarutani was stabbed at about 8.20 p.m. (1120 GMT) about 10 minutes away from his home," the spokesman told Reuters. He said no arrests have been made and no motive had yet been identified for the stabbing.
Yamaichi, the smallest of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages, announced on Monday the resignation of its chairman, president and five vice presidents over suspected payoffs to a racketeer.

The firm is suspected of paying 79 million yen ($681,000) illegally to Ryuichi Koike, the corporate racketeer at the heart of a financial scandal which has also ensnared giant brokerage Nomura Securities and Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB).
More than a dozen people, including top executives from Nomura and DKB, have been arrested in the affair which involved payoffs to racketeers to stop them disrupting annual shareholder meetings.
The months-long scandal involving some of Japan's top financial institutions has led to calls for a major cleanup of business ethics.
It coincided with plans by Japan for a "Big Bang" deregulation of financial markets to make them competitive worldwide.
The police spokesman said Tarutani was stabbed numerous times in the stomach and chest in a parking lot near a railway station in Omori, an inner Tokyo residential area.
Passerbys found Tarutani drenched in blood and slumped on the ground. He was rushed to hospital but died shortly after admittance.
"The lower half of his body was drenched in blood. We talked to him, but his body was shaking and he was in no condition to talk," the owner of a Chinese noodle shop told reporters.
